journal.title: Journal
journal.intro: Every money movement, with its debit and credit lines.

trial.title: Trial balance
trial.intro: Debits and credits per account. The two totals must always be equal.

movements.title: Money movements
movements.intro: Record money that moves between your banks and cash boxes, bills you pay, money the owner puts in or takes out, and other income. Every record gets a voucher number (JV-000123) and shows in the journal and account statements.

approvals.intro: Money going out from {amount} EGP, and every claimed money in (owner capital, other income, merchant payments, merchant balance changes), waits here until a second person approves it. Nobody can approve their own.

opening.title: Opening balances
opening.intro: The balances the books start from on your first day: money in each bank and cash box, what you owe and what is owed to you. Posted once; later corrections are journal entries.

profit.title: Profit by store
profit.intro: Income and costs per dark store, merchant or rider, worked out from every entry. Costs not tied to a store (head office, software) are shown as company wide.

profit.perOrderHint: Tag every expense with its store (Money movements, Expense) so these numbers are right.

payroll.title: Salaries
payroll.intro: Employees on our payroll and people hired through an outsourcing company. The monthly run pays employees from one bank or box after income tax, social insurance and the martyrs fund, and records what is owed to the state. Outsourced people are paid by their company (a monthly bill per person under Suppliers and bills); we only give them advances and bonuses.
payroll.noSalaries: Set salaries first (admin, in the table above).
payroll.outsourcedHint: To mark someone as outsourced, add their outsourcing company under Suppliers and bills first.
payroll.insuredHint: The wage social insurance is counted on (from the contract); empty means the salary.
payroll.bonusHint: Employees get bonuses in the salary run, where they are taxed.
payroll.owedToState: Owed to the state: income tax EGP {tax}, social insurance EGP {insurance} (both shares), martyrs fund EGP {martyrs}.
payroll.noRun: No salary run for this month yet.

payables.ageing: What we owe, by how late

payables.vatOwedHint: VAT charged on our fees minus VAT we paid on bills.
payables.whtOwedHint: Kept back from supplier payments; paid every quarter.
payables.whtReportHint: Payments from {from} to {to}. Enter these lines in the e tax portal (form 41).

payables.noWht: No withholding tax in this quarter.
payables.recurringHint: Each month it waits in Approvals; nothing is paid by itself.

period.yearClosed: Closed with {number}; profit EGP {amount} moved to retained earnings.

refill.title: Automatic refill
refill.intro: Every evening (Settings: refill hour) the system checks each store. A product below its minimum is refilled up to its maximum, from the sorting facility first, then from stores with more than their maximum. The trips wait as drafts until you approve them in Transfers.
refill.noHub: Add a sorting facility in Dark stores and hubs first; refill starts from it.
refill.drafts: {count, plural, =0 {No drafts waiting} one {# draft waiting for approval} other {# drafts waiting for approval}}
refill.alreadyPlanned: Today's refill was already prepared. Approve the drafts in Transfers.
refill.planned: {count, plural, =0 {Nothing is low. No drafts needed.} one {# draft prepared.} other {# drafts prepared.}}
refill.error: Could not prepare the refill. Try again.
refill.badLevels: Use whole numbers, minimum not above maximum. Leave both empty for the store default.

geo.title: Address map
geo.intro: Shiply Now places addresses by reading the area names in them: governorate, district, neighbourhood, compound, then street, each one tighter than the last. Only when the map cannot decide do we pay Google, and every Google answer teaches the map new names for you to approve here.
geo.placed: Last 30 days: {engine} addresses placed by the map, {google} by Google.

import.title: Fill the map from OpenStreetMap
import.intro: Run neighbourhoods and compounds first, then streets. Streets go one district at a time and take about 10 to 20 minutes; keep this page open until it finishes. Running it again updates the same areas.
import.running: {kind}: working, {done} of {total} parts done, {saved} areas saved so far.
import.failed: Not loaded this time (OpenStreetMap was busy): {names}. Run streets again later to fill them.
import.error: The import stopped. OpenStreetMap may be busy; try again in a few minutes.

try.title: Try an address
try.intro: See how the map reads an address, without paying for a lookup.
try.zone: Inside a delivery zone: no Google lookup needed.
try.outside: Outside every delivery zone: no Google lookup needed.
try.unsure: The map is not sure ({reason}), so Google would be asked.

reasons.area_spans_zones: the area crosses a zone border

suggestions.title: Names to approve
suggestions.intro: Words from addresses Google placed inside an area the map did not recognise. Approve to teach the map (you can correct the words first) or reject.

names.title: Add a name by hand
names.intro: Find an area and add another way people write it, in Arabic or English.

sop.title: Help and SOPs
sop.intro: How we work: the steps for your role, written for the screens you use.

store_staff.title: Dark store staff
store_staff.who: Receivers, pickers and packers in a dark store or the hub. Your store opens from Home after you sign in.
day: Start of shift (first 10 minutes): sign in, open your store, read Orders (red = late), check the scanner reads a barcode, check the Receive and Put away counts.
Every hour: Orders first, always. Between orders: put away, then returns and transfers, then counts.
Before a rider leaves: every packed order has its photo and was handed over by scanning the badge.

End of shift (last 15 minutes): receive cash from every rider who is back, put away everything in receiving, receive goods back from failed deliveries, and write a ticket to the next shift lead about anything open.
escalation: An order will be late, or a product is missing on the shelf: tap Missing on the order (admin is alerted automatically) and tell your store lead.
A shipment arrives without a shipment number from the merchant: do not take it; open a ticket to admin with the merchant name and number of boxes.
Cash does not match: enter what you counted; finance reviews it. Do not change the count.
Scanner, phone or internet down for more than 10 minutes: call your store lead; they open an urgent ticket to admin.
Anything you are not sure about: ticket to your store lead before you act.

sections.title: Clock in and out
steps: At the store, open your store's home and tap Clock in at the top. Allow location when the phone asks.
Your phone must be inside the store (within 150 m) with GPS on; the card then shows the time you clocked in and if you were late.
At the end of your shift tap Clock out, also at the store.
check: The card shows Clocked in at the time you arrived; My HR in the Settings menu shows your month.
problems: Too far or not precise enough: step outside or near a window, turn on GPS and try again.
Location blocked: allow location for the site in the browser settings.
Phone dead or forgotten: tell your store lead; HR adds the punch with a reason. A forgotten clock out is closed at your shift end and flagged.

sections.title: Receive a merchant shipment
steps: Ask the driver for the merchant's shipment reference. No shipment in Receive for that merchant means no receiving: call admin.
Open Receive and choose that shipment. Check the merchant name matches the boxes.
Open one box at a time. Scan every unit. Each scan adds 1 to the receiving bin.
Damaged on arrival: put it aside; after closing, report it in Damaged and held with cause Arrived damaged.
When all boxes are empty, tap Close shipment and confirm.
check: The screen shows received against expected for every product.
The shipment's status bar shows Received.
The receiving bin count went up by what you scanned (Put away shows it).
problems: Barcode refused (not in catalog): put the item aside, take a photo of the label, and open a ticket to admin with the merchant name.
More units than expected: receive them anyway; the merchant sees them as extra.
You closed by mistake: tell admin by ticket at once; do not receive the rest on another shipment.

sections.title: Put away
steps: Open Put away. Pick up the units from the receiving bin.
Scan the product, then scan the shelf label where you place it.
Repeat until the receiving bin is empty.
check: Put away on Home shows 0 units to shelve.
The product is on the shelf whose label you scanned.
problems: Shelf full: use the next empty shelf and scan that one.
No shelf label: print it from Bin labels before placing anything there.

sections.title: Pick an order
steps: Open Orders and tap the top order (oldest first, red is late). Tap Accept if it is new.
Go to the shelf shown. Scan the shelf (optional), then each product.
If a product is not there, tap Missing for it. Never replace it with something else.
check: Every line shows picked equal to ordered (or the missing units are marked).
The status bar moves to Picking, then Packed after packing.
problems: Wrong product scanned: the screen refuses it; scan the right one.
Product damaged on the shelf: tap Missing, then report it in Damaged and held with cause Store handling.

sections.title: Pack and hand to the rider
steps: Pack all items, close the bag and stick the order label.
Take a clear photo of the closed bag. Packing does not finish without it.
When the rider arrives, scan the rider's badge.
Give the bags and say the number of bags out loud.
check: The status bar shows Out for delivery.
The rider's screen shows the order with the right number of units.
problems: The screen refuses to add an order to a rider's trip: an order on the trip would be late; give it to another rider.
Wrong badge scanned: call admin; do not let the rider leave with the order.

sections.title: Cash from riders
steps: Open Cash and choose the rider.
Count the money in front of the rider, twice.
Type exactly what you counted and save.
Put the cash in the store box at once.
check: The handover shows Balanced, or Waiting if it differs (finance reviews it).
The store box total in Cash went up by the amount.
problems: Short or over: save the real count anyway, write a note (what the rider said), and the difference goes to finance.
Rider refuses to wait for the count: do not save; tell the store lead.

sections.title: Rider cash limit and petty cash
steps: Home lists the riders holding cash, with the amount and since when. Red means held too long: take their cash in Rider cash now.
If handing over a cash order says the rider is over the cash limit: take their cash first, then scan the badge again. Only a store manager may hand over anyway, with a written reason.
Petty cash: open Petty cash, choose what it was for, type the amount and a note, take a photo of the receipt, and tap Pay from the box.
Keep the paper receipt in the box envelope.
check: The petty expense shows Paid (the box went down) or Waiting for approval (finance decides first).
No rider on Home is red at the end of your shift.
problems: The box does not hold that much: do not pay from your pocket; ask the store lead to call finance.
No category fits: ask finance by ticket to open one; do not choose a wrong one.
Rejected by finance: read the reason on the list and return the money or the item as told.

sections.title: Failed deliveries and returns to merchants
steps: When a rider brings goods back: open the order and tap Receive goods back.
Merchant return: open Returns, choose the return, scan each unit listed.
When ready, hand it to the merchant's driver and type the driver's full name.
check: The order shows the goods are back; the return shows Collected.
problems: Goods not back within 2 hours of a failed attempt: admin gets an alert; find the rider and ask.

sections.title: Damaged stock, counts and transfers
steps: Damaged: open Damaged and held, scan the unit, choose the cause, save.
Count: open Stock count, scan the bin, scan every unit you find; you are not shown the expected number.
Transfer to send: open Transfers, pick by scan, tap Send.
Transfer received: scan every unit into receiving, close it, then put away.
check: Damaged units are no longer on sale.
The count shows Submitted; admin approves differences.
The transfer status bar shows In transit (sent) or Received.
problems: Units for a transfer not found: send what you have; the missing units are released and admin is told.

sections.title: Packaging (bags, boxes, labels)
steps: When you pack, choose the box size if you used one of our boxes; the bag, label and tape of the recipe are taken by themselves.
Use only what the recipe says for that merchant; if an order needed more, tell your store lead.
Once a week (or when admin asks), count the packaging: Inventory, Packaging, Count, choose the item and type the units on the shelf.
check: After packing, the store's packaging stock is lower by what the order used.
The count shows the number you typed.
problems: The screen says the store ran short of packaging: pack anyway with what you have and tell your store lead; admin is alerted.
Packaging is low (alert on Home or in Alerts): your store lead asks finance for a purchase order.

sections.title: Turn on phone notifications
steps: iPhone: open Shiply Now in Safari, tap Share, Add to Home Screen, then always open it from the Home Screen icon (needs iOS 16.4 or later). Android and computers: any browser works; installing the app is optional.
Open the Settings menu (top of every screen), then Notifications.
Tap Turn on notifications on this device and allow notifications when the phone asks.
Tap Send me a test: a notification must appear within a few seconds.
Switch off the kinds you do not need. You are told about: new orders to accept, late orders, shipments and transfers on their way to your store, tickets.
check: The page says notifications are on for this device and the test arrived.
Tapping a notification opens the right screen in Shiply Now.
problems: Blocked: allow notifications for the site in the browser or phone settings, then turn it on again.
No test arrives: check the phone is not in Do Not Disturb or battery saver, then send another test.
A lost or old phone: remove it from Your devices on the same page.

rider.title: Rider
rider.who: Riders delivering 60 minute orders from one dark store.
day: Start of shift: sign in, allow location, check your phone battery is above 50% and you have change for cash orders.
For every trip: take orders only by badge scan at the store; check the number of bags.
After every trip: come back to the store, give back failed goods, and hand any cash over if your lead asks.
End of shift: hand all cash to the store and watch it being counted. Nothing stays with you overnight.
escalation: Customer not answering after the calls the app asks for: mark it failed with the door photo; the store lead decides the next step.
Accident, police or danger: stop, stay safe, call your store lead at once.
Wrong amount of cash collected: type exactly what you got; finance will review it.
App not working: call the store lead; do not hand over a package without the code or a photo.

sections.title: Clock in and out
steps: At your store, open the rider app and tap Clock in at the top. Allow location when the phone asks.
You must be at the store (within 150 m) with GPS on.
When your shift ends and your cash is handed over, tap Clock out at the store.
check: The card shows Clocked in at the time you arrived.
problems: Store says you are not clocked in when handing you an order: clock in first (some stores require it).
Too far or not precise: go to the store, turn on GPS and try again; if it still fails call the store lead.

sections.title: Deliver an order
steps: Open the order and tap Directions.
At the address, call from the app if you cannot find it.
Ask for the 4 digit customer code and type it, or take a photo of the handover.
Cash order: take exactly the amount shown, type what you got, tap Delivered.
check: The order moves to Finished today as Delivered.
Today's cash total went up by the amount.
problems: Code wrong: check it again with the customer; never deliver without the code or a photo.
Customer has no change: do not give change from the company cash; call the store lead.

sections.title: When you cannot deliver
steps: Customer not answering: call from the app as many times as it asks, then take a photo of the door.
Tap Could not deliver, choose the reason, add details if Other.
Bring the goods back to the store on the same trip.
check: The order shows Attempt failed or Failed.
Store staff tapped Receive goods back.
problems: You cannot get back to the store: call the store lead; never keep goods overnight.

sections.title: Cash at the end of the shift
steps: Go to the store with all the cash you collected.
Hand it over and watch it being counted.
Check that the counted total matches your app's total for today.
check: The store's screen shows Balanced.
problems: Difference: tell staff what happened so they write it in the note; finance decides.

sections.title: Turn on phone notifications
steps: iPhone: open Shiply Now in Safari, tap Share, Add to Home Screen, then always open it from the Home Screen icon (needs iOS 16.4 or later). Android and computers: any browser works; installing the app is optional.
Open the Settings menu (top of every screen), then Notifications.
Tap Turn on notifications on this device and allow notifications when the phone asks.
Tap Send me a test: a notification must appear within a few seconds.
Switch off the kinds you do not need. You are told about: orders handed to you, tickets, a late clock in.
check: The page says notifications are on for this device and the test arrived.
Tapping a notification opens the right screen in Shiply Now.
problems: Blocked: allow notifications for the site in the browser or phone settings, then turn it on again.
No test arrives: check the phone is not in Do Not Disturb or battery saver, then send another test.
A lost or old phone: remove it from Your devices on the same page.

merchant.title: Merchant
merchant.who: Shops selling with Shiply Now 60 minute delivery.
day: Every morning: check Orders and Notifications; check stock you are low on in Products.
Before sending stock: create the shipment first, then send.
Every week: check your Wallet and statement; make sure your payout schedule is right.
escalation: A question about an order or money: write to Shiply support (your account manager) with the order or payout number.
Something missing after a shipment was received: reply with the shipment number and the product SKU within 48 hours.

sections.title: Start selling
steps: Add your products (one by one, by file, or by linking your Shopify store). Every product needs a barcode.
Set your 60 minute delivery price in Delivery.
Create your first shipment so we can receive stock.
check: The checklist on Home is all ticked.
problems: A barcode is refused: it already belongs to another product; use the real barcode on the item.

sections.title: Send stock
steps: Shipments, New shipment: list each product and quantity.
Write the shipment number on every box.
Send the boxes to the address shown.
check: The shipment goes Expected, Receiving, Received.
You get a summary: expected against received.
problems: Extra units: they are received and shown as extra; nothing to do.

sections.title: Orders and money
steps: Shopify orders with the 60 minute option arrive by themselves; you can also add one in New order: search the customer's neighbourhood and, if you know the building, drop a pin on the map. The form tells you at once whether the store can take it.
You can cancel only new or accepted orders.
Wallet shows what we owe you; payouts go to your bank on your schedule.
check: Each payout shows a bank reference.
problems: A payout looks wrong: download the statement for the period and send it with your question.

sections.title: Your team
steps: Owners open Team to add the people who work on the account: name, email, password, and owner or member.
Members get only the rights you tick: orders, stock, money, settings.
Someone leaves: Disable them the same day; they are signed out everywhere.
check: A member sees only the menu items of their rights.
problems: You cannot lower or disable yourself, and one active owner always stays: make someone else owner first.

sections.title: Turn on phone notifications
steps: iPhone: open Shiply Now in Safari, tap Share, Add to Home Screen, then always open it from the Home Screen icon (needs iOS 16.4 or later). Android and computers: any browser works; installing the app is optional.
Open the Settings menu (top of every screen), then Notifications.
Tap Turn on notifications on this device and allow notifications when the phone asks.
Tap Send me a test: a notification must appear within a few seconds.
Switch off the kinds you do not need. You are told about: orders delivered or failed, payouts paid, products running low (each only if your rights cover it).
check: The page says notifications are on for this device and the test arrived.
Tapping a notification opens the right screen in Shiply Now.
problems: Blocked: allow notifications for the site in the browser or phone settings, then turn it on again.
No test arrives: check the phone is not in Do Not Disturb or battery saver, then send another test.
A lost or old phone: remove it from Your devices on the same page.

finance.title: Finance
finance.who: The finance team and the accountant. Everything is in Finance.
day: Every morning (30 minutes): Overview; review every cash difference in Cash; deposit yesterday's store cash to the bank (choose the bank, write the slip number).
Payout days: Payouts, prepare due payouts, check each, transfer from the bank, mark paid with the bank reference.
Every bill or money movement the same day it happens: Money movements, with the paper receipt's number as reference.
End of month: trial balance, profit and loss, balance sheet, bank statement check, CSVs to the accountant.
escalation: A rider is short more than once in a week: ticket to admin with the CH- numbers.
A payout bounced or a bank figure does not match: ticket to admin; do not book a correction until you know why.
The trial balance does not balance: stop and open an urgent ticket to admin (it should never happen).

sections.title: Review a cash difference
steps: Cash, Waiting for you: open the handover (CH-...).
Read the note and talk to the store lead if needed.
Write it off (company loss) or keep it on the rider, always with a reason.
check: The handover leaves the waiting list; the rider's cash in Riders is right.
problems: You are not sure who is right: ticket to the store lead; decide only after the answer.

sections.title: Deposit store cash to the bank
steps: Cash, the store, enter the amount and the bank slip number, choose the bank, Deposit.
Keep the slip; write the JV number on it.
check: The store box goes down and the bank account (Chart of accounts) goes up by the same amount.
problems: Deposited to the wrong bank: book a Transfer between the two banks with the reason; never delete.

sections.title: Record money movements
steps: Transfer: from one bank or box to another.
Expense: choose the category and where it was paid from; enter VAT if the bill shows it.
Owner money: capital in or drawings out.
Journal entry: corrections, with a written reason. Debits must equal credits.
check: You get a voucher number (JV-...). Write it on the receipt and file it.
The account statement shows the line with the right balance after it.
problems: Not enough money in the account: the screen refuses; check the date and the account.

sections.title: Merchant payouts
steps: Payouts, prepare due payouts for the day.
Open each draft (PAY-...) and compare with the merchant's statement.
Download the bank transfer file at the top of Payouts and upload it to CIB's bulk transfer (merchants without a bank account are listed; they fill it in their Wallet).
After the bank confirms, Mark paid with the bank reference and the bank used.
check: The payout shows Paid; the merchant's balance dropped by the amount.
problems: Amount looks wrong: cancel the draft with a note and open a ticket to admin.

sections.title: Approvals and receipts
steps: Approvals: every money in claim, and money out from the approval limit, waits here for a second person.
Open each one, check the receipt or bank slip, then Approve or Reject with a reason. You cannot approve your own.
Receipts: attach the photo of the paper receipt or transfer slip to every movement listed there.
check: Approved items get a JV number; the Receipts list gets shorter every day.
problems: Something waits that you never asked for: reject it and open an urgent ticket to admin.

sections.title: Close the month
steps: After the month end checks pass, Close the books through the last day of the month.
Nothing can be posted before that day any more; only someone who manages settings (the owner) can reopen, with a written reason.
check: Close the books shows the new closed through day.
problems: A late bill for a closed month: enter it today with a note; ask admin only if it must sit in the old month.

sections.title: Salaries and advances
steps: Salaries: HR keeps each person's employment (employee or outsourced, with their company) and salary package (basic plus allowances, from a day on). Payroll shows them read only; ask HR for any change.
An advance: choose the person, amount and the bank or box it is paid from.
Month end: choose the month and the bank, enter bonuses, deductions and advances to take back, Check the run (tax, insurance, martyrs fund per person), then Pay; print the payslips.
Outsourced people: enter their company's monthly bill per person in Suppliers and bills; take advances back when paying that bill; pay their bonuses here.
Each month pay salary tax, social insurance and the martyrs fund from Taxes.
check: Each person's advance owed goes down; the run shows in Approvals when it is above the limit.
problems: Someone is missing from the run: HR has not set their salary package yet; ask HR (a ticket to the HR manager).

sections.title: Supplier bills
steps: Suppliers and bills: add the supplier once with their tax id and withholding % (ask the accountant).
New bill the day it arrives: supplier, their invoice number, dates, category, store, amount before VAT and the VAT.
To pay: open the bill, enter the amount, the bank and the transfer reference. The withholding tax is kept back by itself.
Look at What we owe, by how late every week; pay the red columns first.
check: A paid bill leaves Open bills; the supplier's We owe goes to zero.
problems: Bill entered twice or wrong: Cancel bill with a reason (only before any payment).

sections.title: Taxes
steps: Taxes shows the VAT and withholding tax we owe today.
Every quarter: open the quarter, give the list to the accountant for form 41, then Pay tax (withholding) for the total.
Every month: Tax returns gives the VAT return boxes; after the accountant files it, Pay tax (VAT) for the amount filed.
Every month: Tax returns gives the salary tax and insurance lists (CSV); pay both from Taxes.
Every quarter: Tax returns, download the form 41 CSV and upload it to the tax portal.
After the year ends: Tax returns, company income tax; book the amount agreed with the accountant before closing the year.
check: The amount owed goes down by what you paid.
problems: A supplier has no tax id: add it on the supplier before filing.

sections.title: Recurring, prepaid and equipment
steps: Recurring expenses: rent, internet and the like; each month on its day it waits in Approvals.
Prepaid and equipment: rent paid ahead goes in Pay ahead; shelves, fridges and motorbikes in Buy equipment.
Each month end the system moves the right part to the expense or depreciation by itself.
check: Months charged goes up by one every month.
problems: A recurring expense changed price: stop the old one and add a new one.

sections.title: Merchants who owe us
steps: Owed by merchants lists every merchant whose fees passed the cash we collected.
Call them, then Ask to pay (they see it in their panel).
When they transfer, enter it in Merchants as a payment from the merchant.
check: The merchant leaves the list once their balance is back to zero or above.
problems: Owed for more than 30 days: ticket to admin.

sections.title: Bank matching
steps: Every week: download the statement from CIB online banking as Excel (.xlsx) or CSV.
Bank matching, choose the bank, choose the file; check the columns it picked and the first lines, then Import statement.
In the bank, not in the books: bank fees go to Book as bank charges; money that came in is entered as a merchant receipt or owner capital first; a bank error is set aside with a reason.
In the books, not in the bank: find out why (a deposit not made, a cheque not cleared).
check: Both lists are empty and the difference shows Matches.
problems: An entry in the books that never reached the bank after a week: urgent ticket to admin with the JV number.

sections.title: VAT, budgets and cash
steps: VAT report: each month give the accountant the month's line for the VAT return, then record the payment in Taxes.
Budgets: before each month, enter the budget per account (per store or for the company); look at better or worse every week.
Cash flow: read the next four weeks every Monday; if money runs out, tell admin the same day.
check: The forecast's last week ends above zero.
problems: A cost far above budget: ticket to admin with the account and the amount.

sections.title: Year end and exports
steps: In January, after the December checks: Year end and export, Close year for last year (approvers only).
For the accountant: choose the days and Download journal (CSV); it imports into Odoo, Zoho Books, QuickBooks or Daftra.
For the auditor: Download audit pack (zip) with the journal, trial balance, chart of accounts, VAT and receipt photos.
check: The year shows Closed with a JV number; last year's profit and loss still reads the same.
problems: Close the earlier year first: close the years in order, oldest first.

sections.title: Tax invoices and the e-invoice system
steps: First days of each month: Tax invoices, choose last month, Issue the month's invoices.
On the finance PC with the company's USB token: run the signing program (docs/ETA.md); it signs and sends every waiting invoice.
Check that each invoice turns Valid; open a Rejected or Invalid one, fix the reason shown and press Send again.
Giving fees back: open the invoice, Credit note with the amount and reason; a second person approves it.
check: Every invoice of the month is Valid; merchants see them under Invoices.
problems: The signing program shows an error: send the message to admin; do not create the invoices again.

sections.title: Foreign bills, equipment and accruals
steps: A bill in dollars or another currency: choose the currency and the rate on the bill; when paying, type the amount in that currency and today's rate. The difference goes to exchange differences by itself.
Equipment sold or scrapped: Prepaid and equipment, Sell or scrap, with the price (0 if scrapped) and why; a second person approves.
A cost of this month whose bill comes later: Journal entry with Reverse on the 1st of next month.
check: Sold equipment shows Sold or scrapped and stops depreciating.
problems: A rate typed wrong on a bill: cancel the bill (before paying) and enter it again.

sections.title: Cheques
steps: Cheques, Register a cheque: choose Received or Issued and what it is for (merchant balance, security deposit, supplier refund, other income; or a bill, a payout, a deposit paid back), type the printed number, the bank, the amount, the issue and due dates, and attach a photo of the cheque.
A cheque given to us always waits for a second person in Approvals; a cheque we write waits from the approval limit. Until then it shows Waiting for approval.
Every morning look at the Due list: overdue cheques first. Deposit at bank when you hand a received cheque to the bank, Bank paid it when the money shows on the statement (never before its due day).
A cheque came back unpaid: Bounced with the bank's reason. The debt comes back on the merchant, supplier or bill, a payout paid by it is cancelled, and admin gets an alert.
check: Cheques under collection (1151) equals the received cheques not yet cleared; cheques payable (2451) equals the issued ones not yet paid by the bank.
problems: Wrong amount or party: Cancel cheque with the reason (only before it is deposited or cleared), then register it again.
The bill was paid in part meanwhile and the cheque no longer fits: cancel it and write a new one.

sections.title: Merchant contracts, deposits and profitability
steps: Merchant contracts: read each merchant's terms, the deposit we hold and their balance against the credit limit.
Security deposit: Deposit on the merchant's row, Received or Paid back, through our bank or the merchant's balance; a second person approves it.
The monthly minimum is topped up by itself on the 1st for the month before (Monthly minimum top up in the journal and on the invoice).
Profit per merchant: open a month, then a merchant to see fees by kind, costs and margin per order; use What if to try other fees on the same month before talking to the merchant.
check: Deposits held (2600 wallets) match the signed contracts; no merchant shows Over limit without a ticket open with their account manager.
problems: A merchant is over the credit limit and cannot send shipments: ask them to pay, record the receipt, and shipments open again at once.

sections.title: Month end
steps: Trial balance for the month: debits must equal credits.
Profit and loss for the month; balance sheet at the last day.
Compare each bank account statement in Shiply with the real bank statement; book bank charges as an Expense in 5501.
Download the journal and statements as CSV for the accountant.
check: Bank balances in Shiply equal the bank statements.
The balance sheet says Assets equal liabilities plus equity.
problems: A difference you cannot explain: ticket to admin with the account code and the amount.

sections.title: Cash position every morning
steps: Open Accounting, Dashboard, Cash position.
Banks and cash boxes: compare each with the bank app and the store box counts.
Cash with riders: anything Overdue is chased today with the store manager (the store and finance also get a notification).
Owed to merchants shows each merchant's next payout day; bills due within 7 days show what must leave soon. The net position is what is left after both.
Export CSV when the owner asks for the day's position.
check: No rider cash is Overdue by noon.

Reverse a petty expense paid by mistake with a reason (approvers only); the money returns to the box.
After the month ends open Configuration, Month end checklist and choose the month.
Open each item that is not done and finish it: rider cash and differences, bank lines, receipts, petty cash, tax invoices, payroll, storage, depreciation.
Prepare the VAT return in Tax returns, then tick VAT return with a note.
When every item is done, tap Close the books.
check: Every item shows Done (or a tick with a note) and the books are closed through the last day.
problems: An item cannot be finished (for example a day without stock shows storage missing): tick it by hand with a note that explains why.

sections.title: Purchase orders and packaging

Below the approval limit it is approved at once; above it another person with the approve level approves it.
Mark it as sent to the supplier. When goods arrive, enter what came on the order (it can come in parts): packaging goes into the store's stock.
When the supplier's invoice arrives, Make the bill on the order with their invoice number; then pay it from Bills as usual.
Close the order when it is complete, or when the supplier will not send the rest (with a note).
Packaging bought in a shop and paid now: Inventory, Packaging, Buy and pay now, with the receipt photo.
check: The order's status bar shows Billed or Closed and its bill appears under Bills.
Packaging stock value (Inventory, Packaging) equals account 1402 in the trial balance; 2401 is zero once everything received is billed.
problems: The bill is refused as above the order: check the supplier's prices; ask admin to change finance.po_bill_tolerance_bp only if agreed.
Goods came that were not ordered: do not receive them on the order; open a new purchase order.

sections.title: Emails to merchants

A Failed email: check the address with the merchant (they change it in Wallet), then tap Send again.
check: After a payout, two emails show Sent for that merchant within a minute.
problems: The page says email is not set up: tell admin; emails wait until SMTP is configured.

check: The page says notifications are on for this device and the test arrived.

admin.title: Admin

day: Every morning: Overview, then Alerts (handle each one), then Tickets (For me).
Every hour at peak: Orders, late ones first; call the store lead of any red store.
Every evening after 21:00: Transfers, approve or edit tonight's refill drafts.
Every week: Merchants (sign ups), Counts (approve differences), Damage (settle), Settings (check nothing changed by mistake).
escalation: You receive what nobody else can decide: missing stock, money differences, merchant complaints, broken equipment.

HR, Attendance, Today: who is in, late, missing or off at each store. Days: closed days with late, overtime and hours, and a CSV export.
Open a day to correct it: add a punch the phone could not make, void a wrong one, or set the status; every correction needs a reason.
check: Yesterday's days are closed the morning after; a forgotten clock out shows the flag.

sections.title: Stores, hubs and zones

To review: decide each area that was split between two stores (keep, move or not served).
Address map: run the OpenStreetMap import once, then approve the names it learns each week.
check: Try an address on the Address map page: it lands in the right store.
problems: An area belongs to another store: tapping it asks before moving it.

problems: A merchant moved to a new Shopify store: Disconnect store, then link the new one.

sections.title: Merchant contracts

Tiers apply from the order that crosses the band, never to earlier orders of the month; empty values use the fee settings.
With Accounting access, the same page shows this month's fees, costs and margin; Details opens the what if.
check: The merchant sees the contract read only under Contract; the History panel shows every change.
problems: Shipments refused for a merchant over the credit limit: the alert names the balance; finance records the payment or you raise the limit with the owner's agreement.

sections.title: Stock

problems: A count is stale: ask the store to count the bin again.

check: Every file shows 100% documents, a position, a grade and a manager; the org chart has one person at the top.
problems: Manager loop refused: someone would manage themselves through the chain; set the manager on the file instead.

services.title: Everything after the customer taps Buy
services.lead: You sell. We hold the stock, move it, deliver it and bring the money back, with one dashboard that shows every order and every pound.
services.f1p: Your customer chooses the 60 minute option at checkout. The nearest dark store picks the order by scan, packs it with a photo and hands it to a rider. They can follow the rider live on a tracking page.
services.f2p: Send your stock to us once. We count it, shelve it by barcode and keep every store full before it runs low.
services.f3p: Riders collect the exact amount. Every pound is counted at the store and paid into your bank daily, twice a week or weekly.
services.f4p: Stock levels, the 60 minute rate at checkout, an area picker on your store and tracking links, all from one app.
services.f5p: Missed deliveries come back to the store and go out again. When you want stock back, we pick it and hand it over.
services.f6p: Orders, stock per store, wallet, statements and tax invoices in your merchant dashboard, in Arabic or English.

faq.title: Before you send us your first box
faq.a1: A fee per delivered order, a small share of cash collected, and storage per unit. We agree your rates before you start, and every fee shows on your statement.
faq.q2: What if an item is not in the store?
faq.a2: The 60 minute option does not show at checkout for that customer, so they are never promised what we cannot deliver.
faq.q3: What happens when the customer does not answer?
faq.a3: The rider calls, takes a photo at the door and brings the order back. We try again or return it to you, as you choose.
faq.q4: Who sets the delivery price my customer pays?
faq.a4: You do. The 60 minute price is yours and the money stays with you.
faq.a5: Shopify gives you the full connection. You can also create orders by hand from your dashboard.
